title: The Boatwright
logline: A boatbuilder binds eight separate timbers into one hull, testing every lashing, before anyone trusts the finished craft to open water.
human_question: What holds a set of separate, ordinary parts together well enough to carry someone across?

situation.what_happens: A builder takes a commission or a repair and assembles a working craft from parts that are useless alone: timbers selected and shaped, lashings drawn tight, the whole checked for balance. A single weak binding makes the boat unsafe without making it look unsafe, so testing matters more than appearance. It ends with a launch and with someone else's life depending on the work.
situation.who_is_involved: The builder and whoever works alongside them; the fisher or family who commissioned the craft and will take it out; an apprentice learning which bindings can be trusted.
situation.what_is_at_stake: Money for the owner, reputation for the builder, and safety for whoever goes out in it. Also the survival of a way of building that may be nearly gone.
situation.how_it_unfolds: Work runs from selection through assembly to launch, over days or weeks, against the owner's need to be fishing. Pressure comes from timber quality, from cost and from the temptation to accept a binding that is nearly right. It ends at the launch, and the sea decides the rest. Reality decides whether such work is still being done at all.

concept_merge.why_together: C076 (the thirty-seven requisites) contributes the source's own comparison: the eight path factors are like a raft of eight great logs bound together, which carries a person across the ocean [C076-P:L1413], and the digest adds that in the full sense all the factors arise together in a single moment, so human analogies fit only the gradual stage [C076-P:L1467]. C016 (the eight supramundane minds) contributes the term the tradition uses for those minds, explained as what carries one across and beyond [C016-P:L25].
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Together they make a claim about composition rather than effort: what carries someone across is not one strong thing but several ordinary ones that have to hold at once, and the failure of any one is invisible until it matters. The comparison alone would be decorative; the craft alone would be a trade film.

concept_links.why: The source compares the eight path factors to a raft of eight great logs bound together that carries one across the ocean [C076-P:L1413]. The digest cautions that the factors arise together only in a single path-moment and that everyday teamwork analogies cannot reproduce that [C076-P:L1467], so the film shows the physical form and never states the comparison as a lecture.

The source explains the term for the path and fruition minds as what carries one across and beyond the worlds of existence [C016-P:L25]; the craft is one more physical echo of carrying across, with no claim attached.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: What carries a person across is made of separate ordinary parts that only work bound together, and a single weak binding is invisible until the water tests it.
what_must_be_real: A real commission or repair that would happen anyway, and a boat that will actually be used. No construction is revived or staged for the film, and nobody is presented as having attained anything.

risks: Traditional lashed construction may be rare or gone; reviving it for the film would be a fabrication
Letting the comparison be spoken over the images
drop_if: No yard still builds or repairs this way for real use
The only available build would exist because the film asked for it
